title: Polynomial Advice Yields Polynomial-Size Circuits
statement: Every binary language decidable by a finite deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time when given an advice string of length exactly $C(n+1)^d$ for inputs of length $n$, for some natural numbers $C,d$, has a family of Boolean circuits of size at most $a(n+1)^k$ for some natural numbers $a,k$. Each circuit is a well-formed acyclic directed graph of AND, OR, and NOT gates, with each NOT gate having exactly one input and each gate reading at most two earlier vertices.
hypotheses_covered: Some natural numbers $c,C,d$ specify the time bound and advice length.
The advice string has length exactly $C(n+1)^d$ for every input length $n$.
The deciding machine runs in time at most a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ on the paired input.
The circuits have fan-in at most two, are well formed, and have size at most $a(n+1)^k$ for some natural numbers $a,k$.
